mode: read-only source review plus offline synthetic reproduction

points: Record pins id@revision; content_hash covers body+payload, not the complete metadata. Model-authored records require provider/model/prompt_version/run_id.
SourceSpan records exact Python string offsets and the verbatim quote. Generic Record validation is supplemented by commit-boundary existence/domain/role/span checks.
Immutable content-addressed JSON files are published before a chained manifest; only published manifests are readable. A manifest is the atomic visibility boundary.
A root writer lock serializes threads/processes; expected revisions provide CAS; identical idempotency keys reject different contents.
SQLite/FTS is disposable and rebuilt from manifests; the separate runtime queue is not reconstructed from archive text.
Default real TF-IDF char1-4 fitting gives a corpus-specific space, exact cosine baseline, and saved vocabulary/idf; this is lexical embedding, not a neural semantic model.
Generations persist vectors/providers/graph/clusters/themes and switch current by atomic file replacement. Old generations allow rollback, although publication ordering has a confirmed race.
Only event roots become clustering nodes. Interpretation feelings can anchor to one event; raw messages/reflections/states do not become independent cluster events.

Real Leiden runs recursively at resolutions 0.5 and 1.25 with fixed seed; only positive similar edges are clustering weights. Soft theme memberships and provisional labels are separate from Leiden partitioning.
Chinese trigram FTS, archive lexical matches, vector views, explicit event time/person filters, and theme membership fuse through RRF.
Typed graph expansion adds sources/counterexamples. Exact quoted spans travel with raw messages; transitive audit logs can remain versioned pointers under budget.

Persona changes index rationale plus the explicit changed wording/diff; source refs and optional omitted logs remain readable. Historical index mismatch is reported but does not currently prevent future semantic-edge leakage.

confirmed_findings.title: Historical snapshot recall uses semantic relations created after that snapshot
confirmed_findings.trigger: Create two events and save snapshot S. Later commit a contradicts edge between those same events, rebuild current index, then recall at S.
confirmed_findings.actual: The archive at S has zero edge records, but RecallBundle.counter_refs uses the later relation. Endpoint visibility and a watermark warning do not make the relation valid as of S.
confirmed_findings.expected: Historical recall must use a compatible graph/theme generation or exclude relation records not current/visible at the requested snapshot.
confirmed_findings.impact: The past is reinterpreted with a future model assertion, so as-of provenance is inconsistent. No cross-user leak was reproduced.
confirmed_findings.direction_only: Gate graph/theme semantics by selected snapshot. Checking endpoint refs alone is insufficient; check the actual semantic edge record revision, or fall back when generations mismatch.

confirmed_findings.title: An older asynchronous index rebuild can overwrite a newer published current generation
confirmed_findings.trigger: Pause an older rebuild at the real embed call. Commit a second record and finish a newer rebuild. Resume the old one.
confirmed_findings.actual: The lock serializes file writes but does not validate snapshot order. Reopened current points to the older watermark and lacks second@1 vectors.
confirmed_findings.expected: Normal publication should not regress current to an older archive watermark; intentional rollback is a separate API.
confirmed_findings.impact: Committed records are safe, but newer vectors/themes are replaced by an older index until another rebuild. Current lexical fallback reduces data loss but does not restore the overwritten current pointer.
confirmed_findings.direction_only: Under the publication writer lock compare current publication/archive sequence with the candidate and refuse an older normal publication. Preserve explicit rollback semantics.

limitations: 本地 char-ngram TF-IDF 是词面向量基线，不是神经语义 Embedding；否定与跨话题语义能力有限。
群落主题仍为 provisional；算法占位标签不代表 A3 模型语义摘要已验证。
感受视角缺失时跳过并重新归一化可用视角权重；不会伪造感受。
索引水位与请求快照不一致；向量结果仅保留可见 revision，全文与时间/人物从请求快照回退。

targeted_commands.interpretation: Strict expected failures document two confirmed defects; these are not fixed/passing product checks.
Targeted real checks for original-source validation, domain isolation, disposable projection, Windows process CAS/crash recovery, true TF-IDF/Leiden, and index rollback.

limits_not_new_confirmed_defects.point: Hash checks detect accidental/tampered bytes when the recorded checksums disagree. They are not signatures against an attacker who can replace the full archive and recompute all hashes.

V1 reads scan immutable archives and every commit rewrites the projection. Exact vector/kNN baseline and full clustering rebuild are small-scale correctness baselines, not ANN or scalable incremental guarantees.

theme_materials.time_span currently derives from record.created_at, not Event.occurred_at. Explain it as archive-record time unless the interface is changed; imported old events may all have the same creation day.
The audit did not call a model API or infer semantic quality from fixtures. TF-IDF/Leiden were real; concurrency scheduling was instrumented without replacing the underlying algorithms.
